recentItems.title: Hon. Fasiha Hassan, Young Voices and Trust in Democracy at the 69th CPC, 17 Sept 2026
recentItems.description:
Hon. Fasiha Hassan, Member of Parliament of South Africa, joins Parliament TV at the 69th CPC to discuss youth representation and democratic participation.

In this interview, Hon. Hassan discusses:
• Her experience as part of a new generation of Commonwealth parliamentarians
• Engaging with colleagues from different parliamentary systems
• The representation of young parliamentarians at the conference
• What needs to change for young people in political institutions
• The CPC issue that resonated most strongly with her
• Building trust between citizens and Parliament
• Whether inclusion conversations included young people
• An idea from the conference she would take back to Parliament
• Turning connections into practical collaboration after the CPC ends

📅 Recorded: Thursday, 17 September 2026
📍 Cape Town International Convention Centre, South Africa
🎙️ Parliament TV, DSTV Channel 408

recentItems.title: Most Hon. Juliet Holness, Elected CPA Vice-Chairperson at the 69th CPC, 17 Sept 2026
recentItems.description:
Most Hon. Juliet Holness, Speaker of the House of Representatives of Jamaica, joins Parliament TV at the 69th CPC after being elected Vice-Chairperson of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association at the General Assembly.

In this interview, Most Hon. Holness discusses:
• What her election as CPA Vice-Chairperson means for Jamaica and its legislature
• The significance of the role within the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association
• Priorities she hopes to advance in her new position
• Reflections on the 69th CPC and the week in Cape Town
• The future of the CPA and parliamentary democracy across the Commonwealth

📅 Recorded: Thursday, 17 September 2026
📍 Cape Town International Convention Centre, South Africa
🎙️ Host: Xihlamariso Ngoveni, Parliament TV, DSTV Channel 408

recentItems.title: Hon. Morakane Mosupyoe, Green Mace Recognition and the 69th CPC, 17 Sept 2026
recentItems.description:
Hon. Morakane Mosupyoe, Speaker of the Gauteng Provincial Legislature, returns to Parliament TV at the 69th CPC to discuss the Gauteng branch's recognition under the CPA Green Mace Initiative.

In this interview, Hon. Mosupyoe discusses:
• What the Green Mace recognition means for Gauteng
• The branch's commitment to environmental and sustainability excellence
• How Gauteng will leverage this first-cohort award
• Standout moments from the past week for Gauteng
• Actions she wants prioritised by the CPA, Parliament of South Africa and provincial legislatures

recentItems.title: Hon. Alexandra Mendès, Looking Ahead to the 70th CPC in Ottawa, 17 Sept 2026
recentItems.description:
Hon. Alexandra Mendès, Member of Parliament for Canada and Chair of the Canadian Branch of the CPA, joins Parliament TV as the 69th CPC draws to a close and Canada prepares to host the 70th CPC in Ottawa.

In this interview, Hon. Mendès discusses:
• What it means for Canada to host the 70th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference
• What Canada hopes to contribute to the conversation
• Lessons Canada will take from Cape Town
• What should be carried forward from the 69th CPC into the 70th
• Ensuring smaller and larger legislatures have equal influence
• The importance of inclusive platforms for women, small branches and parliamentarians with disabilities in Ottawa

📅 Recorded: Thursday, 17 September 2026
📍 Cape Town International Convention Centre, South Africa
🎙️ Host: Xihlamariso Ngoveni, Parliament TV, DSTV Channel 408

recentItems.title: Hon. Carolyn Harris, Bringing Menopause into the Parliamentary Space at the 69th CPC, 17 Sept 2026
recentItems.description:
Hon. Carolyn Harris, Member of Parliament of the United Kingdom, joins Parliament TV at the 69th CPC following the Global Menopause Caucus side event.

In this interview, Hon. Harris discusses:
• Why menopause belongs on the programme of the 69th CPC
• Why the Global Menopause Caucus describes menopause as a health equity issue
• Her experience raising menopause in the UK Parliament and how the conversation has changed
• Gaps in access to evidence-based healthcare and accurate information
• Recognising the different experiences of women
• Bridging the gap with male legislators
• Why the Commonwealth is an important platform for this conversation
• What meaningful parliamentary action on menopause would look like
• Finding common ground across political and geographical differences
• What parliamentarians should take away from the caucus
• What success would look like over the next few years

📅 Recorded: Thursday, 17 September 2026
📍 Cape Town International Convention Centre, South Africa
🎙️ Host: Tshepo Morie, Parliament TV, DSTV Channel 408
